title: How Grace Gets You to GO
speaker: Pastor Josh Smith
takeaway: Grace propels us outward and upward — enduring suffering for others' glory, sending even the worst sinners to proclaim the boundless riches of Christ, resting on God's love rather than our worthiness, and approaching God's throne with freedom and confidence.

blocks.text: 1. Grace get you to go even if it means suffering

"For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentiles— Surely you have heard about the administration of God's grace that was given to me for you, that is, the mystery made known to me by revelation,as I have already written briefly…I ask you, therefore, not to be discouraged because of my sufferings for you, which are for your glory." -Ephesians 3:1-3, 13
2. Grace gets the worst sinners to go share the Savior

"In reading this, then, you will be able to understand my insight into the mystery of Christ, which was not made known to people in other generations as it has now been revealed "By the Spirit to God's holy apostles and prophets. This mystery is that through the gospel the Gentiles are heirs together with Israel, members together of one body, and sharers together in the promise in Christ Jesus. I became a servant of this gospel by the gift of God's grace given me through the working of his power. Although I am less than the least of all the Lord's people, this grace was given me: to preach to the Gentiles the boundless riches of Christ, and to make plain to everyone the administration of this mystery, which for ages past was kept hidden in God, who created all things." -Ephesians 3:4-9
2 Questions About Sinners Sharing the Savior Answered
#1 Why can the worst sinners share the Savior? Grace is about His love not your worthiness
#2 Why should the Savior be shared? The Savior is boundless in riches
3. By grace you can go to God freely and confidently
"In him [Jesus] and through faith in him we may approach God with freedom and confidence." -Ephesians 3:12
"Let us then approach God's throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need." -Hebrews 4:16
